**Public Childcare as a Local Amenity -- Evidence from Housing Markets**

<details>
  <summary>Abstract</summary>
  <p>
    This paper studies a large-scale reform of public early childcare provision for children under the age of three in Germany’s most populous federal state, North Rhine-Westphalia. From 2006 to 2014, early childcare coverage increased by almost 20 percentage points. To study whether improved access to childcare is capitalized into local housing prices, I exploit sharp and persistent expansions in a matched staggered event-study design, comparing affected Youth Welfare Office areas with matched never-treated areas that are similar in pre-expansion characteristics associated with childcare demand. I find that house prices increase by 1.1\% in the first three years after the expansion, although the estimate is imprecise, and rise to statistically significant 3.4\% four to six years after the expansion. Relative to matched never-treated areas, this corresponds to an increase in house values of EUR 2,619 per additional percentage point of early public childcare coverage.
  </p>
</details>

**Lost in Translation. Information Frictions in School Track Choice -- Evidence from a Randomized Field Experiment** with [Friederike Hertweck](https://sites.google.com/view/friederikehertweck/){target="_blank"}, [Pia Schilling](https://www.piaschilling.com/home){target="_blank"}, and [Moritz Welz](https://www2.wiwi.rub.de/en/persons/moritz-welz-2/){target="_blank"}

<details>
  <summary>Abstract</summary>
  <p>
    In this study, we analyze whether linguistic barriers and a lack of knowledge about the German school system hinders immigrant parents from making an informed choice about their children’s school track. As part of a randomized control trial in a large German state in the school year 2024/25, parents of fourth-graders are provided a (multilingual) mobile application containing useful information on track choice. Different versions of the App will be randomly assigned to elementary schools. *AER Registration: AEARCTR-0011821.*
  </p>
</details>
